cross_references.label: ERISA Civil Enforcement — § 1109 Relief
cross_references.note: § 1109 defines the breach and the remedy (make plan whole); § 1132(a)(2) is the vehicle that brings it to federal court

cross_references.label: Fiduciary Duties (Prudent Expert Standard)
cross_references.note: § 1109 liability attaches when § 1104 duties are breached; the prudent expert standard defines what conduct is a breach

cross_references.label: Liability for Co-Fiduciary Breach
cross_references.note: Fiduciary who knowingly enabled or failed to remedy another's breach is co-liable under § 1105; applies if insider facilitated fraudulent retirement election

cross_references.label: Prohibited Transactions
cross_references.note: § 1106 transactions are prohibited regardless of outcome; fiduciary dealing in plan assets for own account is per se breach without need to prove harm

cross_references.label: ERISA Statute of Limitations
cross_references.note: § 1109 claims: 6 years from last act of breach, 3 years from actual knowledge; fraud tolls; Tibble confirms ongoing monitoring failures extend the period

cross_references.label: DOL Plan Cybersecurity Best Practices
cross_references.note: DOL guidance establishes what a prudent expert fiduciary would do to prevent unauthorized account changes including unauthorized retirement elections; not binding but defines § 1104 'prudent expert' baseline in 2021+ context
